title: PPE is task-specific
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify the hazard (splash, skin exposure, dust, sharps, airborne contamination or impact) before selecting any PPE.
Select gloves and eye protection from the risk assessment, product label, SDS and site requirements, and confirm fit and condition.
Put on and remove PPE without contaminating skin or clean surfaces.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: This lesson develops practical competence in ppe is task-specific for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Choose gloves, eye protection and other PPE from risk assessment, labels and SDS, not from a uniform checklist.

instruction.heading: Prepare and verify
instruction.body: Identify the hazard first: splash, skin exposure, dust, sharps, airborne contamination or impact. Select PPE using the risk assessment, SDS, equipment instructions and site requirements; confirm correct fit and condition.

instruction.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instruction.body: Gloves are not interchangeable. Some products require specific chemical-resistant materials, and respiratory protection requires appropriate selection, fitting and training. PPE is a last layer after safer methods and engineering controls.

instruction.heading: Check, record and escalate
instruction.body: Put on and remove PPE without contaminating skin or clean surfaces. Dispose of single-use items appropriately, clean reusable items and wash hands after removal.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Identify the hazard first: splash, skin exposure, dust, sharps, airborne contamination or impact.
Select PPE from the risk assessment, the label or SDS, the equipment instructions and site requirements, not from a uniform checklist.
Confirm that the glove material suits the product, because gloves are not interchangeable.
Check that each item fits and is in good condition before use.
Use safer methods and engineering controls first, treating PPE as the last layer.
Put on and remove PPE without contaminating skin or clean surfaces.
Dispose of single-use items appropriately, clean reusable items, and wash hands after removal.
Stop and seek direction before using respiratory protection unless you have the appropriate selection, fitting and training.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: The hazard is identified before any PPE is selected.
Gloves and eye protection are chosen from the risk assessment, label, SDS and site requirements.
The fit and condition of PPE are confirmed before use.
PPE is put on and removed without contaminating skin or clean surfaces, and hands are washed after removal.
summary: The hazard, such as splash, skin exposure, dust, sharps, airborne contamination or impact, is identified before any PPE is chosen.
Gloves and eye protection are selected from the risk assessment, product label, SDS and site requirements, and their fit and condition are confirmed.
PPE is put on and taken off without contaminating skin or clean surfaces, and it is the last layer after safer methods and engineering controls.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do before using a respirator you have not been fitted for?
options: Stop, and check with the supervisor before using respiratory protection you have not been fitted and trained for
Borrow a colleague's respirator and use it for the rest of the day in the room with the door shut
Skip PPE, since it is only a last layer and the room is well ventilated and the door is open
Use the respirator nearest to hand, since it looks right for the job and it is in the van already

knowledgeChecks.question: How should missing or damaged PPE be handed over before a task continues?
options: Hand the damaged gloves to the next worker and tell them the gloves are fine to use today
Use the damaged gloves and mention it later at the end of the day with the crew
Keep the PPE issue to yourself and finish the job without telling anyone else
Tell the supervisor which hazard is unprotected and what PPE is needed before the task continues

knowledgeChecks.question: Explain the task-specific decision
options: Use the same gloves for all products, since gloves are gloves in every room
Use the glove nearest to hand, since it is the usual size and it is always in the bag
Choose gloves from the uniform checklist and the colour and style of the uniform
Choose gloves from the risk assessment, label and SDS, and confirm fit and condition

knowledgeChecks.question: Which glove choice is unsafe when the product label specifies the glove type?
options: Choosing gloves that match the material the label requires today
Wearing gloves that are not the chemical-resistant type the label requires
Cleaning reusable gloves between tasks and drying them in the sun
Washing hands after removing gloves and drying them on a towel

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be recorded about PPE issued for a hazardous task?
options: No record is needed because PPE is personal and each worker buys their own
Keep unsuitable PPE on site in case it is needed and label it for the next job
Mention it to the next worker verbally only and not write it down anywhere
Record the PPE issued and any defects, and escalate any PPE that does not suit the hazard
